motivation.iter2_result_precisely: Iteration 2's TRUE sequential replay (_sequential_admit, one position at a time) gave ADAPTIVE_SEQUENTIAL total=$+10,473.20 (n=273) vs the naive derived union $+10,528.60 -- only a $55.40/0.5% gap (13 candidates lost to sequencing), nothing like the filter5_ribbon_fate_2026_07_31.py 86%-pre-emption precedent this whole lane exists to guard against. 7 of 9 frozen gates PASSED, including G1 (recent-25 PRIMARY, $+715.25), G3 (drop-best still positive), G4 (P&L not degraded vs either baseline), and G9 (gain is NOT mostly pre-emption: added cohort n=130/$+3,080.20 vs preempted cohort n=10/-$185.40 -- the identity gain_over_control $2,894.80 == added_total - preempted_total held exactly). It died on exactly TWO gates: G2 (day-majority, 82up/119down, but disclosed as a PRE-EXISTING shape of the ribbon_ride population -- CONTROL_SEQUENTIAL itself already shows the same shape, 48up/69down, informational not adaptive-specific) and, decisively, G5 (Bold's own n=32/$14,539.40 runner cohort, ZERO tolerance): 2 of those 32 trades were individually pre-empted because an earlier qty=3 fallback trade occupied the single position slot, dropping the cohort to $13,493.00.
motivation.diagnosis: The failure mechanism is SLOT CONTENTION, not exit degradation (qty=3's own TP1/runner leg split was re-proven sane at both tiers in iter2's own guard file; exit shape is identical regardless of size). The engine holds exactly ONE position at a time (C11). The unconditional fallback rule spends that scarce slot on EVERY floor-5-unaffordable signal, including marginal ones -- and twice in 386 trading days, that slot was still occupied when a higher-quality, floor-5-affordable signal arrived that would have ridden a runner. The natural fix is to make the fallback SELECTIVE: only spend the slot at reduced size when the setup is good enough to deserve occupying it.
motivation.known_structural_risk_disclosed_up_front: G2 (day-majority) is reused VERBATIM per this iteration's own task charter, but CONTROL_SEQUENTIAL -- the unconditional current-engine baseline, entirely UNAFFECTED by any selectivity rule tested here -- already fails it (48up/69down). Every cell tested below is CONTROL_SEQUENTIAL plus a FILTERED SUBSET of iter2's added trades (selectivity can only shrink the added cohort, never add trades CONTROL didn't already have access to at qty=5). It is therefore expected, on structural grounds stated BEFORE running, that G2 is unlikely to flip to PASS under any selective rule -- a smaller added cohort moves the population's day-shape CLOSER to CONTROL_SEQUENTIAL's own failing shape, not further from it. This is flagged now, as a mechanism-level prediction, specifically so it cannot be mistaken for a post-hoc excuse if it comes true. All gates are still computed and reported honestly regardless of this prediction; the prediction does not exempt any cell from G2.

hypothesis: Restricting the qty=3 fallback (iter2's resolve_bold_qty_adaptive) to fire ONLY on signals that clear an additional, independently-mechanism-justified quality bar will reduce the number of times the fallback occupies the slot on a marginal setup, and therefore reduce or eliminate the runner-cohort pre-emption that sank iteration 2 on G5 -- while retaining enough of the ADDED cohort's participation gain to still clear G1/G3/G4/G9. Expected trade-off, stated before running: a stricter bar shrinks BOTH the pre-emption risk AND the added-cohort gain simultaneously (fewer fallback fires, period) -- the open empirical question is whether any of the three candidate bars below lands in a spot where the pre-emption reduction outpaces the gain reduction AND still fires often enough to be a real mechanism (G10, new this iteration).

candidate_rules._doc: Exactly 3 cells, each chosen on MECHANISM (an existing, already-computed classification or an existing named engine boundary), NOT a swept threshold. No cell's parameter was chosen by looking at this iteration's own outcome data -- each traces to evidence or config that existed BEFORE this study ran. n_cells=3 <= 4, so per the task's own guidance no BH-FDR correction is applied; each cell tests a structurally distinct, independently-motivated mechanism rather than points on one continuous scan. A combination cell (A AND C, or A OR C) is explicitly NOT tested as a 4th cell: by construction of eb.classify_tier (SUPER requires confluence+flip or n>=3 triggers; ELITE requires confluence or sequence) every trigger that produces tier SUPER or ELITE is already a level-tied trigger per rule C's own vocabulary in the overwhelming majority of cases (confluence and sequence_* are BOTH classify_tier inputs AND members of PNL-ATTRIBUTION's level_tied_triggers set) -- so A is expected to be an approximate SUBSET of C, and A-AND-C would collapse to ~A while A-OR-C would collapse to ~C. Testing a 4th cell that is analytically expected to duplicate an existing cell would be exactly the kind of fishing-adjacent padding this study must avoid; the (near-)subset relationship itself is reported as an observation once real data is in, not assumed away.

A_tier_bar.predicate: fallback (qty=3) permitted only when row.tier (eb.classify_tier(triggers_fired), the SAME ordinal classification already computed for every row this tool produces, reused verbatim across every prior tier study in this codebase per that function's own docstring) is SUPER or ELITE.
A_tier_bar.mechanism_and_why_this_cut_not_another: PNL-ATTRIBUTION-2026-07-28.json's own tier breakdown (SAFE-side, engine-fullhist-replay-2026-07-23.json population -- disclosed, not re-derived on Bold's own population in this study) found SUPER ($+5,127.10/37tr, WR .51) and ELITE ($+2,758.20/11tr, WR .73) BOTH robustly positive individually, while LEVEL ALONE was net-NEGATIVE (-$990.45/18tr, WR .28) and TRENDLINE the dominant loser (-$1,830.10/124tr, WR .19) on that same population. SUPER/ELITE is therefore the existing ordinal line this repo's own prior research already drew as the demonstrably-strong-both-individually cut -- not a fresh threshold invented for this study. Excluding LEVEL from this bar (despite LEVEL being nominally 'level-anchored') is itself evidence-based: LEVEL alone underperformed on the cited population.
A_tier_bar.provenance_caveat: The dollar evidence above is SAFE-side (engine-fullhist-replay-2026-07-23.json), not Bold's own population, extrapolated here on the theory that eb.classify_tier's ordinal LOGIC (not the specific dollar outcomes) is account-agnostic shared code -- the exact same function already labels every row this Bold tool produces. Disclosed exactly as iter1/iter2 disclosed the SAFE-side 35/$15,774 runner anchor as inapplicable-as-a-number but the classification machinery as shared.

B_time_of_day_cutoff.predicate: fallback (qty=3) permitted only when entry_time_et >= 12:00:00 ET (noon).
B_time_of_day_cutoff.mechanism_and_why_this_cut_not_another: aggressive/params.json's own config vocabulary already names 11:00-12:00 ET 'midday' as a first-class session boundary (midday_trendline_gate key, confirmed present at line 154, currently false/off but a real named concept in THIS params file, not borrowed from Safe) sitting inside the confirmed entry window entry_no_trade_before_et=09:35 / entry_no_trade_after_et=15:00 (lines 38-39). Noon is the natural, already-named boundary between the morning session and the engine's own 'midday' concept. A slot spent on a reduced-size trade AFTER this boundary has structurally less remaining session (entries close 15:00, time-stop 15:40) in which a full-size floor-5 signal could arrive and be pre-empted -- the opportunity cost the fallback risks is intrinsically lower late in the day. Single pre-registered cutoff, not a swept grid across candidate times.
B_time_of_day_cutoff.provenance_caveat: None -- this is a structural/session-mechanics argument about THIS engine's own entry window, not evidence borrowed from a different account's population.

C_level_anchored.predicate: fallback (qty=3) permitted only when the entry's triggers_fired intersects {'confluence','level_reclaim','level_rejection','sequence_reclaim','sequence_rejection'} -- the IDENTICAL 'level_tied_triggers' vocabulary already defined in analysis/deep-research/PNL-ATTRIBUTION-2026-07-28.json's trigger_class_definition, computed directly from each row's own existing triggers field (no new classification invented).
C_level_anchored.mechanism_and_why_this_cut_not_another: This is the exact mechanism named in this iteration's own task charter: 'level-tied entries are the repo's established profitable cohort: +$6,895/66tr vs -$1,830/124tr trendline-only' (PNL-ATTRIBUTION-2026-07-28.md / FIND-THE-MONEY-SYNTHESIS-2026-07-28.md: LEVEL_tied n=57 $+5,098.05 + BOTH n=9 $+1,796.80 = $+6,894.85 combined vs TL_only n=124 $-1,830.10, same engine-fullhist-replay-2026-07-23.json population). An entry anchored to a real chart level arms a structure stop; a trendline-only entry never does and defaults to a raw premium stop -- the two independent lanes (entry-trigger class and exit-stop-mode class) converge on the identical cohort split in that source study. This is the broadest of the three cuts (includes plain LEVEL tier, which rule A's stricter SUPER/ELITE bar excludes).
C_level_anchored.provenance_caveat: Same SAFE-side-population caveat as rule A: the dollar evidence is engine-fullhist-replay-2026-07-23.json's (Safe), the trigger-vocabulary CLASSIFICATION is shared/account-agnostic code, not re-derived on Bold's own population in this study.

method.selection_mechanics: For each of the 3 candidate rules: selective_candidates = every row with qty==BOLD_MIN_CONTRACTS_PREFERRED (5, unconditional, byte-identical to CONTROL -- the preferred tier is NEVER filtered by any cell) UNION every row with qty==BOLD_MIN_CONTRACTS_FALLBACK (3) whose predicate(row) is True. Rows failing the predicate are excluded entirely from the candidate set (the signal does not trade at all under that cell, same fail-closed convention resolve_bold_qty_adaptive already uses for pure affordability denial -- this is a second, additional denial reason layered on top, not a resize). _sequential_admit (imported unmodified from bold_adaptive_sizing_2026_08_02.py) is then applied to selective_candidates exactly as iter2 applied it to the full 286-row set, producing SELECTIVE_SEQUENTIAL per cell.
